planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; unlike deciduous Plumeria rubra, Bridal Bouquet is evergreen in frost-free climates and blooms nearly year-round, with distinctive elongated, fiddle-shaped leaves quite different from typical plumeria foliage.

directions: Plant cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun. Plumeria pudica, commonly sold as Bridal Bouquet, is a distinctive species with elongated, glossy, dark green, fiddle- or spoon-shaped leaves entirely different from the broad, oval leaves of standard Plumeria rubra hybrids, giving it a unique tropical texture even when not in bloom. Unlike most plumeria, it is evergreen and nearly ever-blooming in frost-free conditions, producing clusters of pure white flowers with a soft yellow throat and a mild, pleasant fragrance almost continuously rather than in a single seasonal flush. It also branches and fills out more readily than many plumeria, forming a fuller, bushier plant at a younger age. In zone 9a it is best grown in a container: bring indoors before temperatures drop into the 40s, since it tolerates cold poorly even compared to other plumeria, and reduce water in winter if kept in a cooler spot. Outdoors in frost-free zones it makes an excellent low-maintenance flowering hedge or specimen.

common_name: Mary Helen Plumeria (Fragrant Golden-Yellow Hawaiian Plumeria)

planting.note: Allow cuttings to dry and callus for 1-2 weeks before planting in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun; Mary Helen is a popular Hawaiian-bred plumeria cultivar with large, bright golden-yellow flowers and a strong, sweet fragrance.

directions: Plant cuttings in extremely well-drained, sandy soil in full sun. Mary Helen is a popular Hawaiian-bred plumeria cultivar prized for large, rounded, deep golden-yellow flowers with a strong, sweet, classic plumeria fragrance, considered one of the best solid-yellow cultivars available for both garden display and lei-making. Like other Plumeria rubra hybrids, it is deciduous in cooler weather, dropping its leaves and going fully dormant in winter, and requires complete dryness during that dormant period to avoid stem rot. Established plants bloom heavily through the warm season with waxy, long-lasting flowers held in clusters at the branch tips. In zone 9a it is best grown in a container: bring indoors dry and leafless once temperatures drop below 40F, store in a frost-free location without watering, and return outdoors in spring as new growth resumes. Excellent drainage is the single most important requirement for healthy plumeria.

Vera Cruz Rose is a widely grown, long-established plumeria cultivar producing rich, saturated deep pink flowers with a lighter blush toward the yellow-white center, carrying a strong, sweet, classic plumeria fragrance that intensifies in the evening. It is one of the more reliably vigorous and free-flowering pink plumeria cultivars, making it a popular choice for both garden specimens and lei-flower production in Hawaii. Like other Plumeria rubra hybrids, it is deciduous in cooler weather, dropping its leaves and going fully dormant in winter, and requires complete dryness during that dormant period to prevent stem rot. In zone 9a it is best grown in a container: bring indoors dry and leafless once temperatures drop below 40F, store in a frost-free location without watering, and return outdoors in spring as new growth resumes.
